newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premium stable to lower, support seen.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premium stable to lower, support seen.

text.p: The Thai physical sugar market remained featureless as buying interest waned, but traders said they expected to see some support soon.

The premiums of Thai raw sugar were stable to lower from earlier this week with March/May delivery, on an FOB basis, quoted at 0.60/0.70 cent a pound over the March futures on New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE).
January/March delivery was quoted at 0.85 cents over the New York futures. The Thai market was packed with offers but no bids, trade sources said.
"Major buyers such as Japan and China are out of the market. News of surpluses in major producing countries also pressured prices," said one trader.
But another trader from a Japanese trading firm here said he expected to see some buying soon as prices were becoming attractive.
"I think there is some demand out there. But buyers are sitting out to see whether the market has bottomed out," he said.
"However, despite some negative fundamentals, I expected to see some support at this level," he added.
Some other traders said Thai raw premiums might be supported by government forecasts expected soon on sugar cane output, which are expected to be bearish.
They said rain and floods were likely to reduce cane output to below previous agriculture ministry forecasts of above 60 million tonnes and could delay crushing, which normally starts early November.
"Perhaps the output will not be bullish as we earlier thought it would be," one trader said.

At port, there was only one new declaration this week for 13,100 tonnes of bagged white sugar for Indonesia. Kerry was said to be a buyer. Market talks put the prices at US$320-325 per tonne on an FOB basis.
Vessel Yala Navee was scheduled to leave a Thai port on Thursday with 17,650 tonnes of bulk raw sugar to Japan. Kerry and Tate & Lyle were buyers.
Tate & Lyle also bought 1,000 tonnes of white sugar for Singapore, 1,600 tonnes for South Korea and 1,000 tonnes for Cambodia. All were scheduled to be shipped within this month.
C.F. bought 500 tonnes of white sugar for Cambodia. The vessel Lucky Four was scheduled to be ready by October 15.
